summary: Cold Bay Airport (CDB/PACD) is a strategically located medium airport on the Alaska Peninsula, historically serving as a critical refueling stop and emergency diversion field for military and trans-Pacific aircraft since World War II. Its exceptionally long runway, originally built by the military, remains one of the largest in Alaska and can accommodate wide-body jets. Today it serves the small community of Cold Bay while still functioning as an important diversion airport for trans-Pacific routes.
faqs:
Q: What is Cold Bay Airport primarily used for today?
A: The airport serves the local community of Cold Bay on the Alaska Peninsula and continues to function as a designated emergency diversion field for trans-Pacific flights, thanks to its exceptionally long runway built during the military era.

Q: Does Cold Bay Airport have scheduled passenger service?
A: Yes, limited regional passenger flights operate to Cold Bay, connecting the community to Anchorage and other Alaska hubs, typically using turboprop aircraft.

Q: What is special about Cold Bay's runway?
A: The runway is approximately 10,000 feet long, making it one of the longest in Alaska and capable of handling large commercial and military aircraft, which is why it serves as a trans-Pacific diversion airport.

Q: Is Cold Bay Airport near any notable natural attractions?
A: Yes, it is the gateway to the Izembek National Wildlife Refuge, renowned globally for its enormous migratory bird populations and stunning wilderness landscapes.
transport_tips: Cold Bay is remote and has no road connection to the mainland road system, so nearly all visitors arrive by air. Ground transportation options are extremely limited, so arranging a rental car or shuttle in advance through local providers is strongly recommended. The airport operates on Alaska Time and weather-related delays are common due to frequently foggy and windy conditions.
local_tip: Bring binoculars and extra camera storage—Cold Bay is one of the world's premier birding destinations, and the short drive from the airport into Izembek National Wildlife Refuge offers some of the best black brant and emperor goose viewing
